questions.stem: A 55-year-old man takes part in a research study. He has an arterial line and echocardiography before and 10 minutes after a single IV drug. Before the drug: pulse 72/min, blood pressure 118/76 mm Hg, left ventricular end-diastolic volume (EDV) 120 mL, and end-systolic volume (ESV) 50 mL. After the drug: pulse 60/min, blood pressure 156/98 mm Hg, EDV 124 mL, and ESV 74 mL. Which drug was most likely given?
choices: Dobutamine
Esmolol
Nitroprusside
Phenylephrine
Normal saline bolus
questions.explanation: Stroke volume fell from 70 mL to 50 mL, and ejection fraction fell from about 58% to 40%, while blood pressure rose and ESV rose. This is the pressure-volume pattern of higher **afterload**, which **phenylephrine** causes through **α1** vasoconstriction; the lower pulse is a **baroreceptor reflex**. **Esmolol** also raises ESV and lowers the pulse, but by lowering contractility, so blood pressure would fall, not rise.
questions.explanation_pt: O volume sistólico caiu de 70 mL para 50 mL, e a fração de ejeção caiu de cerca de 58% para 40%, enquanto a pressão arterial e o volume sistólico final (VSF) subiram. Esse é o padrão pressão-volume de aumento da **pós-carga**, que a **fenilefrina** causa por vasoconstrição **α1**; a queda da frequência cardíaca é um **reflexo barorreceptor**. O **esmolol** também eleva o VSF e reduz o pulso, mas por reduzir a contratilidade, então a pressão arterial cairia, e não subiria.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old woman who had rheumatic fever as a child has 1 year of shortness of breath on exertion. At the cardiac apex, the first heart sound is loud. Shortly after the second heart sound there is a sharp, high-pitched extra sound, followed by a low-pitched rumble in diastole. The short silent interval between the second heart sound and the extra sound corresponds to which phase of the cardiac cycle?
choices: Isovolumetric relaxation
Isovolumetric contraction
Rapid ventricular filling
Reduced ejection
Atrial systole
questions.explanation: **S2** marks aortic valve closure, which starts **isovolumetric relaxation**: all valves are closed and left ventricular pressure falls with no change in volume. The **opening snap** is the stiff mitral valve opening, which ends this phase. **Rapid ventricular filling** starts only after the mitral valve opens, so it begins at the snap, not before it. A higher left atrial pressure opens the valve earlier, so a shorter S2-to-snap interval suggests more severe **mitral stenosis**.
questions.explanation_pt: A **B2** marca o fechamento da valva aórtica, que inicia o **relaxamento isovolumétrico**: todas as valvas estão fechadas e a pressão do VE cai sem mudança de volume. O **estalido de abertura** é a abertura da valva mitral rígida, que encerra essa fase. O **enchimento ventricular rápido** só começa depois que a mitral abre, ou seja, no estalido e não antes dele. Uma pressão atrial esquerda maior abre a valva mais cedo, então um intervalo B2-estalido mais curto sugere **estenose mitral** mais grave.

questions.stem: A 59-year-old man has 6 months of episodes of facial flushing and watery diarrhea. CT shows several masses in the liver, and urinary 5-HIAA is high. His pulse is 84/min and regular. There is a holosystolic murmur at the left lower sternal border that gets louder with inspiration. The liver edge pulses with each heartbeat. Which jugular venous pulse finding is most likely?
choices: Absent a waves
Cannon a waves that appear at irregular intervals
Large c-v wave with loss of the x descent
Absent y descent with pulsus paradoxus
Deep x descent with a small v wave
questions.explanation: Serotonin from **carcinoid** liver metastases reaches the right heart and causes fibrosis of the **tricuspid valve**, leading to **tricuspid regurgitation**. Blood flows back into the right atrium during ventricular systole, so the systolic x descent is replaced by a **large c-v wave**, which is also felt as a **pulsatile liver**. Absent a waves are typical of **atrial fibrillation**, and his regular pulse makes that unlikely. An absent y descent with pulsus paradoxus is the pattern of **cardiac tamponade**.
questions.explanation_pt: A serotonina das metástases hepáticas do **tumor carcinoide** chega ao coração direito e causa fibrose da **valva tricúspide**, levando à **insuficiência tricúspide**. O sangue reflui para o átrio direito durante a sístole ventricular, então o descenso x sistólico é substituído por uma **onda c-v proeminente**, também percebida como **fígado pulsátil**. A ausência de onda a é típica da **fibrilação atrial**, e o pulso regular torna isso improvável. Ausência de descenso y com pulso paradoxal é o padrão do **tamponamento cardíaco**.

questions.stem: A 66-year-old man with chronic kidney disease started spironolactone 3 weeks ago. He now has muscle weakness. Serum studies show sodium 136 mEq/L, potassium 7.6 mEq/L, bicarbonate 18 mEq/L, and creatinine 3.9 mg/dL. ECG shows peaked T waves, flat P waves, and a wide QRS complex. Which change in the ventricular myocyte action potential best explains the wide QRS?
choices: Faster K efflux that shortens the phase 2 plateau
More Ca entry through L-type channels during phase 2
Block of the delayed rectifier K channels that slows phase 3 repolarization
Larger funny current that makes phase 4 steeper
Less negative resting potential, inactivating fast Na channels
questions.explanation: High extracellular K makes the **resting membrane potential less negative**. At this potential many **fast Na channels** stay inactivated, so the **phase 0** upstroke is slower and the impulse spreads slowly through the ventricles, which widens the QRS. High K also increases K conductance and speeds **repolarization**, which explains the **peaked T waves**, not the wide QRS. QRS width depends on phase 0 conduction, not on the plateau.
questions.explanation_pt: O K extracelular alto torna o **potencial de repouso menos negativo**. Nesse potencial, muitos **canais rápidos de Na** ficam inativados, então a despolarização da **fase 0** fica mais lenta e o impulso se propaga devagar pelos ventrículos, o que alarga o QRS. O K alto também aumenta a condutância ao K e acelera a **repolarização**, o que explica as **ondas T apiculadas**, e não o QRS largo. A largura do QRS depende da condução na fase 0, não do platô.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old woman has a dobutamine stress echocardiogram. As the infusion rate rises, her left ventricle contracts more strongly. It also relaxes faster in early diastole, and the isovolumetric relaxation time becomes shorter. Which molecular event best explains the faster relaxation?
choices: Opening of ryanodine receptors on the sarcoplasmic reticulum
Phosphorylation of phospholamban, releasing SERCA
Inhibition of the Na/K ATPase, which raises intracellular Na
Higher calcium affinity of troponin C
Opening of more L-type Ca channels in the T tubules
questions.explanation: β1 stimulation raises cAMP and activates **protein kinase A** (PKA). PKA phosphorylates **phospholamban**, which removes its brake on **SERCA**, so the sarcoplasmic reticulum takes Ca back faster and the muscle relaxes sooner (**lusitropy**). More **L-type Ca channel** opening is also a PKA effect, but it increases Ca in systole and explains stronger contraction, not faster relaxation. PKA also phosphorylates troponin I, which lowers, not raises, the Ca affinity of troponin C.
questions.explanation_pt: A estimulação β1 aumenta o AMPc e ativa a **proteína quinase A** (PKA). A PKA fosforila o **fosfolambano**, que deixa de inibir a **SERCA**, então o retículo sarcoplasmático recapta o Ca mais rápido e o músculo relaxa antes (**lusitropismo**). A abertura de mais **canais de Ca tipo L** também é efeito da PKA, mas aumenta o Ca na sístole e explica a contração mais forte, não o relaxamento mais rápido. A PKA também fosforila a troponina I, o que reduz, e não aumenta, a afinidade da troponina C pelo Ca.

questions.stem: A healthy 24-year-old man does a treadmill test. At rest: pulse 68/min, blood pressure 118/76 mm Hg, and cardiac output 5.0 L/min. At peak exercise: pulse 172/min, blood pressure 182/72 mm Hg, and cardiac output 19 L/min. Which mechanism best explains why his diastolic blood pressure did not rise?
choices: Higher venous return from the skeletal muscle pump
Resetting of the carotid baroreceptors to a lower pressure
β1-mediated increase in myocardial contractility
Metabolite-induced arteriolar dilation in working muscle
Sympathetic vasoconstriction of skeletal muscle arterioles
questions.explanation: Working muscle releases **local metabolites** (adenosine, K, CO2, H+, lactate) that dilate its arterioles and override sympathetic tone there. **Total peripheral resistance** falls a lot: mean arterial pressure divided by cardiac output goes from about 90/5.0 = 18 to about 109/19 ≈ 5.7 mm Hg·min/L. So the much higher cardiac output raises systolic pressure, but diastolic pressure stays about the same. The **muscle pump** raises venous return and cardiac output, which would push pressure up, not keep diastolic pressure down.
questions.explanation_pt: O músculo em atividade libera **metabólitos locais** (adenosina, K, CO2, H+, lactato) que dilatam suas arteríolas e superam o tônus simpático local. A **resistência vascular periférica total** cai muito: a pressão arterial média dividida pelo débito cardíaco passa de cerca de 90/5,0 = 18 para cerca de 109/19 ≈ 5,7 mm Hg·min/L. Assim, o débito muito maior eleva a pressão sistólica, mas a diastólica fica praticamente igual. A **bomba muscular** aumenta o retorno venoso e o débito, o que elevaria a pressão, e não manteria a diastólica baixa.

questions.stem: A 22-year-old man feels lightheaded and faints while his blood is drawn. He wakes up within 30 seconds. His pulse is 42/min, and ECG shows sinus bradycardia. Which change in SA node cells best explains his slow heart rate?
choices: More K efflux and less funny current, so phase 4 is flatter
Inactivation of fast Na channels, so the phase 0 upstroke is slower
More Ca entry through L-type channels, so the plateau is longer
Block of K channels, so phase 3 repolarization is delayed
Higher cAMP, so the funny current is larger and phase 4 is steeper than normal
questions.explanation: Acetylcholine acts on **M2 receptors** (Gi). The G protein opens **acetylcholine-activated K channels**, so the cell is more negative at the start of phase 4. Lower **cAMP** reduces the **funny current (I_f)**, so **phase 4** rises more slowly and threshold is reached later. Higher cAMP with a steeper phase 4 is the **sympathetic** (β1) effect, which speeds the heart. SA node cells do not use fast Na channels for phase 0.
questions.explanation_pt: A acetilcolina age nos **receptores M2** (Gi). A proteína G abre **canais de K ativados por acetilcolina**, então a célula fica mais negativa no início da fase 4. O **AMPc** menor reduz a **corrente funny (I_f)**, então a **fase 4** sobe mais devagar e o limiar é atingido mais tarde. AMPc maior com fase 4 mais inclinada é o efeito **simpático** (β1), que acelera o coração. As células do nó sinusal não usam canais rápidos de Na na fase 0.

questions.stem: A 50-year-old woman has a right heart catheterization to evaluate shortness of breath. Her oxygen consumption is 300 mL/min. Oxygen content is 19 mL O2/dL in arterial blood, 13 mL O2/dL in the superior vena cava, and 14 mL O2/dL in the pulmonary artery. What is her cardiac output?
choices: 4.0 L/min
5.0 L/min
6.0 L/min
7.5 L/min
10.0 L/min
questions.explanation: The **Fick principle** needs **mixed venous** blood, which is blood from the **pulmonary artery**, where venous return from the superior vena cava, inferior vena cava and coronary sinus is fully mixed. CO = 300 mL/min ÷ (190 − 140 mL O2/L) = 300 ÷ 50 = **6.0 L/min**. Using the superior vena cava sample gives 300 ÷ 60 = 5.0 L/min, which is wrong because that blood comes only from the upper body.
questions.explanation_pt: O **princípio de Fick** exige sangue **venoso misto**, que é o sangue da **artéria pulmonar**, onde o retorno da veia cava superior, da veia cava inferior e do seio coronário já está totalmente misturado. DC = 300 mL/min ÷ (190 − 140 mL O2/L) = 300 ÷ 50 = **6,0 L/min**. Usar a amostra da veia cava superior dá 300 ÷ 60 = 5,0 L/min, o que é errado porque esse sangue vem só da parte superior do corpo.
